summary_zh: 學會用 If we…, would you…? 這種假設語氣在會議和電話裡委婉地跟供應商談價格、交期與條件。

vocab.definition: a written statement of how much a product or job will cost
vocab.example: The vendor sent us a quote for 10,000 boxes this morning.
vocab.example_zh: 供應商今天早上寄了一萬個盒子的報價單給我們。

vocab.definition: the time between placing an order and receiving it
vocab.example: The lead time is six weeks, so we need to order now.
vocab.example_zh: 交貨要六週，所以我們現在就得下單。

vocab.definition: a lower price you get for buying a large amount at once
vocab.example: If we ordered 20,000 units, would they give us a bulk discount?
vocab.example_zh: 如果我們訂兩萬個，他們會給我們大量採購折扣嗎？

vocab.definition: to accept part of what the other side wants so that you both give something up
vocab.example: We can't pay the full price, but we could meet them halfway.
vocab.example_zh: 我們沒辦法照原價付，但可以跟他們各退一步。

vocab.definition: the most you will pay or the least you will accept before you refuse a deal
vocab.example: Our bottom line is $1.35 per box; we can't go any higher.
vocab.example_zh: 我們的底線是一個盒子 1.35 美元，不能再高了。

vocab.definition: to make a price or agreement fixed so that it cannot change later
vocab.example: Let's lock in this price before material costs go up.
vocab.example_zh: 趁原料成本上漲前，我們先把這個價格鎖定。

vocab.definition: not able to be changed or discussed
vocab.example: The delivery date is non-negotiable because the store opens that week.
vocab.example_zh: 交貨日沒有商量餘地，因為店就在那週開幕。

vocab.zh: 退出談判；放棄這筆交易
vocab.definition: to stop negotiating and refuse to make the deal
vocab.example: If the price went any higher, we would walk away.
vocab.example_zh: 如果價格再高，我們就不談了。

reading.title: How We Saved the Packaging Deal
paragraphs: Last month, our team kicked off a project to redesign the packaging for our tea gift sets, and my manager, Kevin, asked me to handle the vendor side. Our usual supplier, Brightpak, sent a quote of $1.50 per box for 10,000 boxes, with a lead time of eight weeks. The problem was that the launch was only seven weeks away, and our budget was $1.30 per box.

Before the call, Kevin and I agreed on our bottom line: no more than $1.35, and the boxes had to arrive by March 1. That date was non-negotiable, because the shops had already planned their displays around it. "If they said no to both," Kevin asked, "would we walk away?" I said we probably would, although the only other supplier we knew was much less reliable.

On the call, I tried a different approach. Instead of just asking for a lower price, I said, "If we ordered 20,000 boxes instead of 10,000, would you give us a bulk discount?" The sales manager, Sandra, paused and then offered $1.32. She couldn't shorten the lead time on her own, but she promised to check with the factory.

The next day, she came back with an offer to meet us halfway: they would ship by February 25 as long as we paid 30 percent up front. Kevin signed off on it that afternoon, and we locked in the price for a full year. The project is back on track, and I've given the warehouse a heads-up that the extra 10,000 boxes will need space.
Kevin's comment afterwards stuck with me: "If every negotiation went like this, my job would be a lot easier."

questions.q: Why couldn't the team accept Brightpak's first offer?
options: The boxes would arrive too late, and the price was over budget.
Brightpak could only make 10,000 boxes.
Kevin did not like the new box design.
Brightpak asked them to pay everything up front.
questions.explain_zh: 第 1 段：交貨要 eight weeks，但上市只剩 seven weeks；報價 $1.50 也高於預算 $1.30。

questions.q: How did the writer get Sandra to lower the price?
options: By saying another supplier was cheaper
By offering to order twice as many boxes
By asking Kevin to call Sandra
By agreeing to a later delivery date
questions.explain_zh: 第 3 段：作者問「If we ordered 20,000 boxes instead of 10,000, would you give us a bulk discount?」，Sandra 才降到 $1.32。

questions.q: What does Kevin suggest when he says, "If every negotiation went like this, my job would be a lot easier"?
options: He wants the writer to take over his job.
Most negotiations are harder than this one was.
He did not enjoy this negotiation.
He plans to negotiate with Brightpak again soon.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題。If + 過去式, would… 是假設語氣，表示「現實中並非每次都這麼順利」，也就是大部分談判都比這次難。

grammar.point_zh: 第二類條件句：假設現在或未來不太可能、不真實的情況

guide.key_zh: If 子句用過去式、主要子句用 would＋原形：談的是「假設」，不是已經決定的事

uses.label_zh: 假設跟現況相反或不太可能的事
uses.form: If + S + V-ed, + S + would + V（原形）
uses.signal: if we had…, if they lowered…

uses.form: If + S + V-ed, + would + S + V（原形）?
uses.note_zh: 比 If we order…, will you…? 更委婉、留有餘地

uses.form: If I were you, + I would + V（原形）
uses.note_zh: 固定說法用 were；口語也聽得到 was

mistakes.wrong: If we would order more, they would give us a discount.
mistakes.right: If we ordered more, they would give us a discount.
mistakes.why_zh: if 子句用過去式，would 只放在主要子句

mistakes.wrong: If they lowered the price, we will sign today.
mistakes.right: If they lowered the price, we would sign today.
mistakes.why_zh: if 子句用過去式，主要子句要配 would，不用 will

mistakes.wrong: If I were you, I will ask for it in writing.
mistakes.right: If I were you, I would ask for it in writing.
mistakes.why_zh: If I were you 後面的主要子句用 would（或 could／might）＋原形，不用 will

examples.en: If we had a bigger budget, we wouldn't need to negotiate so hard.
examples.zh: 如果我們預算多一點，就不用這麼辛苦地談了。

examples.en: If we ordered 20,000 boxes, would you give us a bulk discount?
examples.zh: 如果我們訂兩萬個盒子，你們會給我們大量採購折扣嗎？

examples.en: If I were you, I would ask for the quote in writing.
examples.zh: 如果我是你，我會請他們提供書面報價。

exercises.q: If the vendor ___ (lower) the price, we would sign the contract today.
exercises.explain_zh: 假設情況，if 子句用過去式：lowered。主要子句已經是 would sign。

exercises.q: If I ___ (be) you, I would ask for a longer warranty.
exercises.explain_zh: 給建議的固定說法是 If I were you；口語也常聽到 If I was you。

exercises.q: If we paid 30 percent up front, ___ you ship the order a week earlier?
exercises.explain_zh: 談判時試探條件：If + 過去式, would you…? 用 could you 也可以，語氣同樣委婉。

exercises.q: We ___ (not / need) this meeting if the supplier answered our emails.
exercises.explain_zh: if 子句是過去式 answered（實際上他們沒回信），主要子句用 would not + 原形：wouldn't need。

exercises.q: Our budget is fixed. If they asked for more money, we ___ to find another supplier.
options: would have
have
would had
will have
exercises.explain_zh: if 子句是過去式 asked → 主要子句用 would + 原形 have。would 後面不能接 had；have／will have 要配 If they ask（現在式）。

exercises.q: "If we had more time, we would compare more suppliers." What does this mean?
options: We don't have much time, so we can't compare many suppliers.
We had more time last year.
We will compare more suppliers next week.
We have enough time to compare more suppliers.
exercises.explain_zh: 第二類條件句說的是跟現況相反的假設：其實「現在沒有更多時間」，所以沒辦法比較更多供應商。

review.point: Future forms: will, going to, present continuous for plans
review.point_zh: 未來式：will、be going to、現在進行式表示已排定的計畫

exercises.q: I ___ (meet) the vendor at 2 p.m. tomorrow. It's already in my calendar.
exercises.explain_zh: 已經排進行事曆、有確定時間的安排 → 現在進行式 am meeting 最自然；am going to meet 也可以。

exercises.q: "These samples look heavy." "Don't worry, I ___ (help) you carry them."
exercises.explain_zh: 看到狀況當下決定、主動提議幫忙 → will help。

exercises.q: We decided last week to change suppliers. We ___ ask three companies for quotes.
options: are going to
would
are
had
exercises.explain_zh: 事先已經決定的打算 → be going to + 原形：are going to ask。would 是假設；are／had 後面不能直接接原形 ask。

guide.key_zh: 看這件事「決定」的時間：早就排進行事曆、之前就決定了，還是說話當下才決定

uses.label_zh: 已經排進行事曆、跟人約好的安排
uses.signal: on Monday at ten, next week
uses.note_zh: 時刻表（班機、會議系統排程）也可以用現在式：The meeting starts at 10.

uses.label_zh: 之前就決定的打算，或看著證據做的預測
uses.signal: I've decided…, Look at the numbers…

uses.label_zh: 說話當下才決定、答應別人、一般預測
uses.signal: I think…, Don't worry…, OK, I'll…

mistakes.wrong: I will meet the client tomorrow at ten. It's in my calendar.
mistakes.right: I'm meeting the client tomorrow at ten. It's in my calendar.
mistakes.why_zh: 已經排進行事曆的安排，用 be + V-ing 最自然；will 聽起來像現在才決定

mistakes.wrong: Don't worry, I will to send the slides tonight.
mistakes.right: Don't worry, I'll send the slides tonight.
mistakes.why_zh: will 後面直接接原形動詞，不加 to

timeline.label: We're kicking off the project on Monday.
I'm going to keep the meeting short.
OK, I'll send you the agenda now.

listening.title: A Call About the Price

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Hi Marcus, thanks for getting back to me so quickly. Just a heads-up: we're finalizing our budget this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: No problem. Did you have a chance to look at our quote?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: I did. To be honest, $2.10 per bag is more than we can pay. If you could bring it down to $1.80, we'd have a deal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: That's tough. If we dropped the price that much, we'd be losing money on every bag.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: I understand. What if we ordered twelve months of stock at once? Would that change things?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: It might. For an order that size, I could probably do $2.00. But the lead time would go up to six weeks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Six weeks is too long. Our new store is opening on April 3, and that date is non-negotiable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Okay, how about this? I'll ship half the order in three weeks and the rest later. Can we meet halfway at $1.90?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: That works for me, but I'll need to run it by my manager, Kevin. He's going to want it in writing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Of course. I'll send you an updated quote this afternoon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Great. And I'll ask Lily in the warehouse to get up to speed on the split delivery. I owe you one, Marcus.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Happy to help. Talk soon.

questions.q: What price does Marcus finally suggest?
questions.explain_zh: Marcus 最後說「Can we meet halfway at $1.90?」，剛好是 Rachel 要的 $1.80 和他提的 $2.00 的中間。$2.10 是原報價。

questions.q: Who will prepare for the split delivery?
options: Marcus
Kevin
Lily
Rachel
questions.explain_zh: Rachel 說「I'll ask Lily in the warehouse to get up to speed on the split delivery」。Marcus 負責寄新報價，Kevin 是要核准的主管。

questions.q: Why does Marcus offer to ship half the order in three weeks?
options: Because his factory can only make half the order
So that Rachel's new store can open on time
Because Kevin asked for a smaller order
So that Rachel will pay $2.10
questions.explain_zh: 推論題。Rachel 說六週太久，新店 4 月 3 日開幕、日期不能改；Marcus 接著提出先出一半，就是為了趕上開幕。

dictation: If we dropped the price that much, we'd be losing money on every bag.
That works for me, but I'll need to run it by my manager, Kevin.
He's going to want it in writing.

shadowing: If we ordered twelve months of stock at once, would that change things?
Our new store is opening on April 3, and that date is non-negotiable.
I'll need to run it by my manager.

prompts.question: In a meeting, a vendor's price is too high. Make a "what if" offer in one sentence.
prompts.question_zh: 會議中，供應商的報價太高。用一句「如果我們…，你們會…嗎？」提出條件（打字或小聲說都可以）。
prompts.sample: If we ordered twice as many, would you give us a better price?

prompts.question: Your manager asks when the vendor call is. It's already scheduled for Thursday at 10. Answer in one sentence.
prompts.question_zh: 主管問你什麼時候跟供應商通電話。已經排在星期四十點，用一句話回答。
prompts.sample: I'm talking to them on Thursday at ten.

writing.task: A vendor has sent you a quote that is too expensive and too slow. Write an email of 80-150 words to the sales manager, Sandra. Thank her, explain the problem, and make one or two "what if" offers.
writing.task_zh: 供應商寄來的報價太貴、交期也太長。寫一封 80–150 個英文字的 email 給業務經理 Sandra：先道謝、說明問題，再用假設語氣提出一兩個條件。
writing.sample:
Hi Sandra,

Thank you for sending the quote so quickly. We really like the samples, but there are two problems. First, $1.50 per box is above our budget. Second, a lead time of eight weeks is too long, because our launch is in seven weeks.

I'd like to suggest two options. If we ordered 20,000 boxes instead of 10,000, would you be able to offer a bulk discount? And if we paid part of the order up front, could your factory ship a week earlier?

If the numbers work, we would be happy to lock in the price for the whole year. Could we talk on the phone this Thursday?

Best regards,
Mimi
checklist_zh: 開頭先謝謝對方的報價
清楚說明價格和交期兩個問題
用 If we + 過去式, would you…? 提出條件
結尾提出下一步（約時間通話）

translation.zh: 如果我們一次訂兩萬個，你們願意給我們大量採購折扣嗎？
translation.en: If we ordered 20,000 at once, would you give us a bulk discount?
alt: If we ordered 20,000 at a time, would you give us a bulk discount?
If we ordered 20,000 at once, would you be willing to give us a bulk discount?

translation.zh: 如果我是你，我會先要一份書面報價。
translation.en: If I were you, I would ask for a written quote first.
alt: If I were you, I'd ask for a written quote first.
If I were you, I'd get a written quote first.

translation.zh: 我明天早上十點要跟供應商開會（已經排好了）。
translation.en: I'm meeting the vendor at ten tomorrow morning.
alt: I'm meeting the supplier at 10 tomorrow morning.
I'm meeting with the vendor at ten tomorrow morning.

translation.zh: 我建議我們先把這個價格鎖定。
translation.en: I'd suggest that we lock in this price first.
alt: I'd suggest locking in this price first.
I'd suggest that we lock this price in first.
I suggest we lock in this price first.

reading.title: Why the First Number Matters
paragraphs: Anyone who has sat across the table from a supplier knows the feeling: you need the deal more than they do, and they know it. Without much leverage, it's tempting to accept whatever is on the table. Experienced buyers, however, rarely do. Instead, they treat every quote as an opening move rather than a final answer.

One reason is a phenomenon psychologists call anchoring. The first number mentioned in a negotiation tends to pull everything that follows toward it. If a vendor opens at $50,000, a counteroffer of $40,000 suddenly feels bold, even if the job is really worth $35,000. That's why many negotiators try to put a number on the table first, as long as they've done enough research to back it up. Lowball too aggressively, though, and you risk insulting the other side before the conversation has really started.

The second habit is trading rather than simply giving things up. A concession given away for free tends to be pocketed and forgotten; one exchanged for something else keeps the balance even. Rather than just agreeing to a higher price, a skilled buyer might say, "If we accepted that figure, would you extend the payment terms to sixty days?" Phrased this way, the request sounds hypothetical, which gives both sides room to explore without committing.

Finally, good negotiators know how to sweeten the deal without spending money. A longer contract, a public case study, or a quick decision can matter more to a vendor than a few extra dollars. A supplier that is trying to hit a quarterly target, for instance, might drop its price for a buyer who can sign before the end of the month.

None of this means driving a hard bargain at every turn. Suppliers remember how they were treated, and a relationship squeezed too tightly this year may cost you next year, when you badly need a rush order filled overnight.

questions.q: According to the article, why might a counteroffer of $40,000 feel bold?
options: Because $40,000 is more than the job is worth
Because the vendor's first number of $50,000 has become the reference point
Because buyers usually accept the first quote
Because the buyer has no research to back it up
questions.explain_zh: 第 2 段講 anchoring：第一個數字會把後面的討論拉向它。對方先開 $50,000，所以 $40,000 相比之下顯得很大膽，即使工作其實只值 $35,000。

questions.q: Why does the writer like the question "If we accepted that figure, would you…?"
options: It forces the vendor to lower the price immediately.
It lets both sides explore an option without making a firm promise.
It shows the buyer has no other choice.
It ends the negotiation quickly.
questions.explain_zh: 第 3 段：這樣問聽起來是假設，「gives both sides room to explore without committing」，雙方可以探討而不必馬上承諾。

questions.q: What does the last paragraph imply?
options: Buyers should always drive a hard bargain.
Suppliers rarely remember difficult customers.
Pushing a supplier too hard now could hurt you later.
Rush orders are usually filled overnight.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題。最後一段說供應商會記得你怎麼對待他們，今年逼得太緊，明年你急需趕單時可能就會付出代價。

listening.title: Five Minutes Before the Call

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Okay, so before we dial in, what's our opening number?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: I was thinking we anchor at forty thousand. If they came back with forty-five, we'd still be under budget.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Forty? Hmm, isn't that a bit of a lowball? Their last quote was fifty-two.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: Sure, but they've got a quarterly target to hit. I'd bet they're more flexible than they're letting on.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Maybe. But if I were them, I'd be pretty annoyed by…

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: By a number that low, yeah, I get it. So what if we sweetened the deal a bit? Say, a two-year contract instead of one?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Now that's something they'd actually want. A longer contract would matter more to them than a few thousand dollars.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: Exactly. And we'd only make that concession if they threw in free shipping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Right, trade, don't give. Oh, and Ethan? Let me do the talking on price. You tend to fold the second they push back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: Ouch. Fair enough. I'll handle the delivery schedule, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Deal. Okay, it's two o'clock. Let's do this.

questions.q: Why does Ethan think the vendor might accept a lower price?
options: They have a quarterly target to hit.
Their last quote was a mistake.
Olivia has worked with them for years.
They have just lost another big client.
questions.explain_zh: Ethan 說「they've got a quarterly target to hit」，所以認為對方比表面上更有彈性。

questions.q: Who will discuss the price on the call?
options: Ethan
Olivia
Both of them
The vendor's manager
questions.explain_zh: Olivia 說「Let me do the talking on price」，Ethan 則負責交貨時程（I'll handle the delivery schedule）。

questions.q: What does Olivia mean by "trade, don't give"?
options: Never agree to anything the vendor asks for.
Only make a concession if you get something in return.
Offer free shipping to the vendor.
Let the vendor make the first offer.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題。她是在回應 Ethan「只有對方給免運，我們才讓步（簽兩年）」，意思是讓步一定要換到東西。

dictation: If they came back with forty-five, we'd still be under budget.
A longer contract would matter more to them than a few thousand dollars.

glossary.definition: power or advantage that helps you get what you want in a negotiation

glossary.zh: 定錨（先拋出數字影響對方）
glossary.definition: to set a first number that the rest of a negotiation is measured against
to offer a price that is unfairly or unrealistically low
something you agree to give up or accept in order to reach a deal
to add something to an offer to make it more attractive
to give up or give in, especially under pressure
